page: Microsoft Azure L80s_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized server belonging to the Lsv4 family. It features 80 vCPUs and 40 physical cores with 2 threads per core, powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The system includes 640.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.0 GB of memory per core. It is equipped with 19199 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable. The virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. There are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

The server demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, highlighted by a top-tier Geekbench multi-core score of 21672.0 and a strong PassMark CPU score of 79652.77. Memory performance is robust, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 5387.5 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 94.58 GB/sec. Database and web-serving operations are highly efficient, achieving a top-tier static web serving throughput of 105.75 GB/sec and 91.92 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Single-core performance is average, as shown by stress-ng single-core and bzip3 single-threaded decompression benchmarks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L80s_v4 offers high resource density by bundling massive local storage of nearly 19 TB with a substantial memory footprint of 640 GB. This makes it highly qualitative for data-intensive workloads that would otherwise require expensive external storage attachments. However, the lack of dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, though it maintains strong CPU-based LLM inference speeds, such as 275.51 tokens per second for medium 7B model prompt processing.

This server is designed for large-scale database systems, high-throughput web serving, big data analytics, and memory-intensive applications. It is well-suited for Redis deployments, software compilation, and workloads requiring high-speed local storage access.
